section.title: Introduction
section.para: The Research-Development-Loop (RDL) is an orchestrator skill that drives development tasks through a six-phase lifecycle: Research, Brainstorm, Plan, Develop, Verify, and a scholarly review, with a systematic-debugging back-edge. As originally authored, the chain delegated the method of several phases to a specific third-party plugin, Superpowers, by invoking its skills by name (superpowers:systematic-debugging, superpowers:verification-before-completion, and others) and by declaring that its sub-skills inherit the superpowers process verbatim. This bound the chain's correctness to the presence of one plugin.

This paper documents the decoupling of the RDL chain from that plugin. The governing decision, taken by the user, was inline standard and credit: remove the plugin as a required runtime dependency, inline a verified industry standard as the method of each phase, and retain the plugin as a credited compatible reference implementation. The success criterion is behavioural, not cosmetic: the loop must run to completion with the Superpowers plugin absent.

section.title: Two kinds of coupling
section.para: A grep for the token superpowers across the chain returned 51 matches in 13 files, but these fell into two structurally different classes that demand different remedies.

listitem.para: Runtime-invocation coupling — imperative invocations of superpowers:<skill> as required phase steps, and the inherits the superpowers process dependency claims in the two sub-skills. This is the load-bearing coupling: it makes the plugin a hard dependency.

Path/name coupling — the hardcoded default docs_dir = "docs/superpowers" baked into the manifest scaffold and echoed in several references. Cosmetic, but it embeds the plugin's name into every scaffolded project's output path.

section.para: A grep-clean result is not the same as a decoupled result: a skill can stop saying superpowers while still structurally requiring the plugin. The operative test is whether the loop still runs with the plugin uninstalled. This was captured as a guardrail (test_no_hard_superpowers_invocation) that rejects any imperative invocation or inheritance phrasing while permitting credit phrasings.

section.title: Industry-standard replacements
section.para: Each idiosyncratic dependency was mapped to a standard that was web-verified against an authoritative source before being written into a skill, in accordance with the chain's own truth-type gate (a claim supported only by training-data recall is a Q entry, not a verified K entry).

row.entry: structured requirements elicitation and design-review gate; EARS, RFC 2119, C4/Structurizr, MADR (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148)
Work-Breakdown Structure plus Requirements Traceability Matrix plus TDD (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148; Beck)
Root-Cause Analysis — 5 Whys / Ishikawa (ASQ) — plus a failing regression test
Definition of Done (Scrum) plus Verification and Validation (IEEE 1012)
Agent Skills open format (agentskills.io) plus a frontmatter schema and lint script

section.title: The recursive dependency: skill authoring
section.para: Because the task was itself a revision of the skills, the skill-authoring path (Phase 5's route to fixing skill gaps, originally superpowers:writing-skills and skill-creator) was a recursive dependency of the loop: decoupling Phases 0–4 while leaving the self-modification path bound to the plugin would have been an incomplete cut. The substitute is the Agent Skills open format, a real open standard (originally developed by Anthropic, adopted across roughly forty agent products, with an authoritative specification at agentskills.io). Its frontmatter rules are machine-checkable: name is kebab-case (^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$, at most 64 characters, no leading, trailing, or consecutive hyphen) and description is at most 1024 characters and must state both what the skill does and when to use it.

These rules are enforced by a new, dependency-free linter (scripts/lint_skill.py) with a declarative JSON-Schema companion (references/skill-frontmatter.schema.json). The linter is self-hosting: all six chain skills pass it. This makes the loop able to validate its own skill edits without any external plugin.

section.title: The capability manifest
section.para: The chain is governed by an rdloop.toml manifest under a zero-ambient- authority model (every capability denied unless explicitly granted) with the usability relation capability = granted and present. During this work the project's own manifest was corrected to practise what the chain preaches: the dependency standard was moved from the custom last-resort opt-in to PEP 621 with a real pyproject.toml, and the Phase-5 toolchain (xmllint, xsltproc, jing) was granted in [capabilities].subprocess after the scholarly-review phase revealed it had never been declared (see the companion review).

section.title: Verification
section.para: The work was executed test-first. The test suite grew from 54 passing tests to 83 passing tests with zero failures and zero collection errors. New guardrails assert the structural properties that matter: no hard plugin invocation remains; the industry standards are named as the actual method; the base-manifest default no longer embeds the plugin name; every chain skill passes the Agent Skills linter; the discretionary-deferral loophole is closed; and the Phase-5 toolchain is declared and granted.
